objective: Qualify SDR color metadata and bounded LUT import
flags: LUT effects follow YAMAKAN_EFFECTS_OFF=1 and LUT imports YAMAKAN_AG_DOCS_OFF=1; the color policy itself has no switch (it corrects every render)
deviations: Policy sdr-bt709-tv/v1 is frozen and applies to every render: each picture is converted once, explicitly, to BT.709 limited range (yuva420p) and the export is tagged; render compiler v2 and renderer version 4 re-key plans and preview caches once
Before (measured): renders were untagged and converted with FFmpeg's default BT.601 matrix; an HD player reading them as BT.709 showed pure green 253 as 214
Source color is recorded in the import probe record; assets imported earlier are read by the policy's file-type and height defaults, not re-probed
Refusal is an allow-list: HDR (PQ, HLG, Dolby Vision or HDR10 side data), BT.2020 and other gamuts, non-SDR transfers and unconvertible matrices; untagged HDR without side data cannot be detected
LUTs are a creative document kind (lut), parsed from .cube into a 16-bit table; the render writes canonical .cube text into its own folder; the original file is never used

tests/preview.test.ts compares reference and export frames by full-range BT.709 luma (the grayscale reduction weighed an RGB preview by BT.601), and the rendered-opacity tolerance is 8 levels (one BT.709 limited-range chroma step moves pure red by about 1.8 levels)

performance.method: 10 s of 1280x720 at 30 fps, median of 3 exports on Windows
performance.note: lut3d tetrahedral runs single-threaded because renders run filters on one thread by design; threading it is a follow-up

tests.result: 8 color tests: an 8-patch chart round-trips within 5 levels from an RGB still, limited-range BT.709, full-range and untagged SD video, in export, read as BT.709, and in the reference preview, tagged bt709/tv; PQ, HLG, BT.2020, linear, P3 and YCgCo (tags in the H.264 VUI) refused; HDR side data detected; tampered recorded tags map only to policy enums; per-layer policy; a real JPEG and an asset without recorded color; identity and inverting LUTs in export and preview, canonical round trip; a LUT keeps a half-transparent overlay's alpha; the editor's transform keeps the LUT; undo; malformed, huge, include-carrying, out-of-range and 1D LUTs, the generic commit, foreign, stale and double LUT effects and in-use re-import refused
